title.rendered: The Wisdom of the Cross: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: The message of the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God. The wisdom of the world cannot understand. The mind of Christ can.

content.rendered:
The message of the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to those of us who are being saved it is the power of God. The wisdom of the world cannot understand. The mind of Christ can.

The Gospel For Today | Saturday, June 27, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“For the message of the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God… For the foolishness of God is wiser than human wisdom, and the weakness of God is stronger than human strength.”
1 Corinthians 1:18, 25 (NIV)

Today’s Message

Paul writes 1 Corinthians 1 to a church that was being impressed by Greek philosophy. Corinth was a sophisticated city. Their rhetoricians could argue circles around any preacher. Their philosophers had theories about everything. And the cross of Christ, Paul knew, made no sense to any of them. A crucified Messiah was a contradiction in terms. The strongest God revealed in the weakest moment. The wisest God acting in what looked like the most foolish way possible.

Paul does not apologise for the offence. He embraces it. He says the cross is supposed to look like foolishness to the world. That is the point. If salvation came through human wisdom, then human wisdom would be the saviour. The cross is designed to bypass human cleverness and go straight to the heart. The cross is the place where God refuses to play by the world’s rules. The cross is the great reversal where weakness defeats strength, where death conquers death, where the apparent loser turns out to be the only winner.

For the mind of the believer, this matters. The world keeps insisting that real wisdom looks like power, success, control, self-promotion and winning. The cross says no. Real wisdom looks like a Saviour laying down His life for the people who were rejecting Him. Real strength looks like the Son of God submitting to the Father unto death, even death on a cross. Real victory looks like an empty tomb three days later. The wisdom of the cross is the wisdom that overturns the categories of the world.

This is why the believer’s mind cannot be at home in the wisdom of the age. The age says climb. The cross says descend. The age says protect yourself. The cross says give yourself away. The age says win. The cross says die that others may live. The believer who has been to the cross can never look at success the way the world looks at it again. Something has shifted permanently.

And the most beautiful part of Paul’s argument is the end. The foolishness of God is wiser than human wisdom. The weakness of God is stronger than human strength. What looked like the lowest moment in history, the death of an innocent Jewish carpenter outside Jerusalem, was actually the moment that broke the back of sin, death and the devil. The world is still trying to catch up to the wisdom that was on display that afternoon.

So today, when the wisdom of the age tries to talk you out of the cross-shaped life, remember Paul. The message of the cross is the power of God. To you. To me. To everyone who is being saved.

Prayer

Father, I bow before the wisdom of the cross. Where the world calls strength, Your Son chose weakness. Where the world calls winning, Your Son chose dying. And in His death and resurrection, You have saved me. Help me think with the wisdom of the cross today. Help me live with the wisdom of the cross today. Conform my mind to the mind of the Crucified and Risen Lord. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

The message of the cross is not foolishness to me. It is the power of God in my life. I live by the wisdom of the cross. The world’s wisdom is not my master. The Crucified and Risen Lord is my wisdom, my righteousness, my sanctification and my redemption.
